Medicine-01.question: ১) Remittent fever occurs in
Medicine-01.exp:
Remittent fever is classically seen in typhus fever. In remittent fever, the temperature remains elevated throughout the day but shows fluctuations of more than 1°C without returning to normal.

  • Typhus: Typically produces a remittent fever pattern due to systemic infection caused by Rickettsia species.

  • Typhoid: Classically causes a step-ladder fever pattern (gradual rise in temperature).

  • Acute tonsillitis: Usually causes continuous fever, not a typical remittent pattern.

  • Rheumatic fever: Causes intermittent fever but is not classically described as remittent fever.

Exam Pearl:
Remittent fever → Typhus.
Step-ladder fever → Typhoid.

Medicine-01.question: ২) Fever with drenching night sweat is found in
Medicine-01.exp:
Fever with drenching night sweats is a classic B symptom of lymphoma (especially Hodgkin lymphoma). These constitutional symptoms include:

  • Unexplained fever

  • Drenching night sweats

  • Unintentional weight loss (>10% in 6 months)

They indicate increased disease activity and have prognostic significance in lymphoma.

  • Myeloma: May cause bone pain, anemia, renal impairment, and hypercalcaemia; B symptoms are less characteristic.

  • Aplastic anaemia: Presents with pancytopenia (fatigue, bleeding, infections), not drenching night sweats.

  • Leukemia: Can cause fever and night sweats, but the classic association with drenching night sweats as a B symptom is lymphoma.

Exam Pearl:
B symptoms (fever + night sweats + weight loss) → Lymphoma.

Medicine-01.question: ৩) Fever with chill and rigor that subsides with sweating
Medicine-01.exp:
Malaria classically presents with intermittent fever with chills and rigor followed by sweating. This occurs due to the rupture of infected red blood cells and release of parasite products, causing periodic fever paroxysms.

Typical malaria fever pattern:

  1. Cold stage: Chills and rigor

  2. Hot stage: High fever

  3. Sweating stage: Fever subsides with profuse sweating

  • Septicaemia: May cause fever with chills and rigors, but the classic cyclical pattern is not typical.

  • Acute pyelonephritis: Causes fever with chills, flank pain, and urinary symptoms.

  • Subphrenic abscess: Can cause swinging fever but not the classical rigor–sweating cycle.

Exam Pearl:
Fever + chill + rigor + sweating → Malaria.

Medicine-01.question: ৪) Patient feeling feverish with excessive sweating
Medicine-01.exp:
A patient feeling feverish with excessive sweating is a classic feature of thyrotoxicosis due to increased metabolic activity and heat intolerance. Excess thyroid hormones increase basal metabolic rate, causing increased heat production, sweating, palpitations, weight loss, and anxiety.

  • Hypothyroidism: Causes cold intolerance, reduced sweating, weight gain, and lethargy.

  • Diabetes insipidus: Causes polyuria and polydipsia due to impaired ADH action, not excessive sweating.

  • Lymphoma: Can cause night sweats (B symptoms), but not typically a feeling of heat intolerance with excessive sweating.

Exam Pearl:
Heat intolerance + excessive sweating + weight loss → Thyrotoxicosis.

Medicine-01.question: ৫) Fluent aphasia with poor comprehension & good repetition in
Medicine-01.exp:
Transcortical sensory aphasia presents with:

  • Fluent speech

  • Poor comprehension

  • Good repetition (key distinguishing feature)

It resembles Wernicke’s aphasia, but unlike Wernicke’s aphasia, the ability to repeat words and phrases is preserved because the arcuate fasciculus and perisylvian language areas remain intact.

  • Wernicke’s aphasia: Fluent speech + poor comprehension + poor repetition.

  • Broca’s aphasia: Non-fluent speech + good comprehension + poor repetition.

  • Transcortical motor aphasia: Non-fluent speech + good comprehension + good repetition.

Exam Pearl:
Fluent + poor comprehension + preserved repetition = Transcortical sensory aphasia.

Medicine-01.question: ৬) HTN with radiofemoral delay indicates
Medicine-01.exp:
Hypertension with radiofemoral delay is a classic sign of coarctation of the aorta. In this condition, narrowing of the aorta (usually near the ligamentum arteriosum) causes:

  • Delayed and weak femoral pulse compared with radial pulse

  • Hypertension in upper limbs

  • Lower blood pressure in lower limbs

  • Development of collateral circulation (e.g., intercostal arteries)

  • Renal artery stenosis: Causes secondary hypertension but does not produce radiofemoral delay.

  • Polycystic kidney disease: Causes hypertension due to renal involvement but no pulse delay.

  • Cushing’s syndrome: Causes hypertension due to cortisol excess but normal peripheral pulses.

Exam Pearl:
Radiofemoral delay + upper limb hypertension = Coarctation of aorta.

Medicine-01.question: ৭) Fever with rash at 5th day indicates
Medicine-01.exp:
Fever with rash appearing around the 5th day is classically associated with typhoid fever. The rash is called rose spots—small, faint, pink macules seen mainly on the trunk, usually appearing during the second week of illness (often around day 7–10, but may begin earlier).

  • Dengue: Rash commonly appears around the 3rd–5th day, often with thrombocytopenia, myalgia, and bleeding tendency.

  • Typhus: Causes fever with rash, but the rash usually appears after several days and is more generalized.

  • Measles: Rash appears after 3–5 days of fever but is associated with cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.

Exam Pearl:
Typhoid fever → Rose spots (classically on trunk).
Dengue → Fever + rash around day 3–5 with severe myalgia.

Medicine-01.question: ৮) Left iliac fossa mass commonly indicates all of the following excepts
Medicine-01.exp:
A left iliac fossa (LIF) mass commonly arises from pathology involving the sigmoid colon. Important causes include:

  • Diverticular mass (diverticular phlegmon): Common cause of LIF mass, especially in older adults.

  • Sigmoid colon cancer: Can present as a palpable LIF mass.

  • Crohn’s disease: Can cause an inflammatory mass, usually involving the terminal ileum but may present as an abdominal mass.

Constipation may cause fecal loading and abdominal discomfort, but it is not a common cause of a true LIF mass.

Exam Pearl:
Left iliac fossa mass → Think sigmoid colon pathology (diverticular mass, sigmoid cancer).

Medicine-01.question: ৯) Colicky central abdominal pain in a patient with surgical scar mostly indicates
১০) Prune juice like vaginal discharge is found in
Medicine-01.exp:
Prune juice-like vaginal discharge is classically described in dysfunctional uterine bleeding (DUB), especially due to old retained blood mixed with cervical mucus, giving a dark brown/“prune juice” appearance.

  • PID: Usually presents with purulent vaginal discharge, pelvic pain, fever, and cervical motion tenderness.

  • Ruptured ectopic pregnancy: Presents with acute abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, shock, and not typically prune juice-like discharge.

  • Salpingitis: Causes mucopurulent discharge with pelvic pain and fever.

Exam Pearl:
Prune juice-like vaginal discharge → Dysfunctional uterine bleeding (DUB).

Medicine-01.question: ১১) Relieving factor in acute pancreatitis
Medicine-01.exp:
The characteristic relieving factor in acute pancreatitis is leaning forward. Patients often find relief by sitting up and bending forward because this position reduces tension and irritation of the inflamed pancreas and decreases pressure on surrounding structures.

  • Leaning forward: Relieves pancreatic pain (classic feature).

  • Sitting upright: May help because it often involves leaning forward, but the specific classic answer is leaning forward.

  • Eating food: Usually worsens pain by stimulating pancreatic enzyme secretion.

  • NSAIDs: Do not relieve acute pancreatitis pain and may worsen gastrointestinal complications.

Exam Pearl:
Acute pancreatitis pain → Worse after meals, relieved by leaning forward.

Medicine-01.question: ১২) Which is the best means of detecting ascites
Medicine-01.exp:
Ultrasonography (USG) is the best initial and most commonly used investigation for detecting ascites. It is highly sensitive, non-invasive, inexpensive, and can detect even small amounts of free fluid in the abdomen.

Advantages of USG:

  • Detects small-volume ascites

  • Helps identify the distribution of fluid

  • Can guide ascitic fluid aspiration (paracentesis)

  • Useful in evaluating underlying liver disease

  • X-ray: May show signs of large ascites but is not sensitive.

  • CT scan: Can detect ascites but is not used routinely due to cost and radiation exposure.

  • MRI: Not a routine investigation for ascites detection.

Exam Pearl:
Best initial investigation for ascites = Ultrasonography (USG).

Medicine-01.question: ১৩) Drugs that precipitates scurvy excludes
Medicine-01.exp:
Scurvy occurs due to vitamin C deficiency, leading to impaired collagen synthesis. Some drugs can precipitate scurvy by interfering with vitamin C metabolism or increasing its requirement.

Drugs associated with scurvy include:

  • Aspirin → increases vitamin C excretion and reduces tissue vitamin C levels

  • Indomethacin → NSAID; may interfere with vitamin C metabolism

  • Carbamazepine → can increase vitamin C requirement/metabolism

Tetracycline is not classically associated with causing scurvy, so it is the exception.

Exam Pearl:
Drug-induced scurvy → Aspirin, Indomethacin, Carbamazepine.

Medicine-01.question: ১৪) Causes of under nutrition & weight loss in adults due to impaired energy storage
Medicine-01.exp:
Diabetes mellitus causes undernutrition and weight loss due to impaired energy storage and utilization. In uncontrolled DM, deficiency of insulin prevents glucose uptake into cells, causing:

  • ↓ Glucose utilization

  • ↓ Glycogen and fat storage

  • ↑ Lipolysis and proteolysis

  • Weight loss despite normal or increased appetite

  • Thyrotoxicosis: Causes weight loss mainly due to increased metabolic rate and energy expenditure, not impaired energy storage.

  • Cancer: Causes weight loss due to cachexia (inflammatory cytokines and increased catabolism).

  • Pheochromocytoma: Causes weight loss due to increased catecholamine activity and metabolism.

Exam Pearl:
Weight loss due to impaired energy storage → Diabetes mellitus (insulin deficiency).

Medicine-01.question: ১৫) Most common cause of chronic or relapsing diarrhoea
Medicine-01.exp:
The most common cause of chronic or relapsing diarrhoea is Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS), particularly IBS with diarrhoea (IBS-D). It is a functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by recurrent abdominal pain associated with altered bowel habits, without structural abnormalities.

  • IBD (Inflammatory Bowel Disease): Causes chronic diarrhoea but is less common than IBS; usually associated with blood in stool, weight loss, and inflammatory markers.

  • Entamoeba infestation: Can cause chronic diarrhoea/dysentery but is less common.

  • Giardiasis: Causes chronic foul-smelling diarrhoea and malabsorption, especially after contaminated water exposure.

Exam Pearl:
Most common cause of chronic/recurrent diarrhoea → IBS.

Medicine-01.question: ১৬) Rubbing the buttock & thigh describes
১৭) Chest pain with burning chest indicates
Medicine-01.exp:
Burning chest pain is a classic symptom of GERD due to the reflux of acidic gastric contents into the oesophagus, causing heartburn. It is often aggravated by meals, lying down, or bending forward and may be relieved by antacids.

  • AMI (Acute Myocardial Infarction): Causes severe crushing/pressure-like central chest pain, often radiating to the left arm, jaw, or neck.

  • UA (Unstable Angina): Causes ischemic chest discomfort, typically pressure or tightness rather than burning.

  • SVT: May cause palpitations, chest discomfort, and dizziness but not typically burning pain.

Exam Pearl:
Burning retrosternal chest pain → GERD (heartburn).

Medicine-01.question: ১৮) Headache that is severe in morning & associated with projectile vomiting
১৯) Recurrent vertigo with progressive hearing loss & persistent tinnitus is found in
২০) Fever with chill and rigor, Pleuritic chest pain & Cough
Medicine-01.exp:
Fever with chills and rigor, pleuritic chest pain, and cough are classic features of pneumonia. Infection of the lung parenchyma causes inflammation and consolidation, leading to:

  • Fever with chills and rigor (especially in bacterial pneumonia)

  • Productive cough with sputum

  • Pleuritic chest pain due to involvement of pleura

  • Crackles and bronchial breathing on examination

  • Bronchial asthma: Causes wheeze, dyspnoea, and cough but not typically fever with rigor.

  • COPD: Causes chronic cough and breathlessness; fever may occur during exacerbations but pleuritic pain and rigor suggest infection.

  • Lung abscess: Causes fever and cough with foul-smelling sputum, but is less common and usually follows aspiration or severe infection.

Exam Pearl:
Fever + chill/rigor + pleuritic chest pain + cough → Pneumonia.

Medicine-01.question: ২১) ‘Mumble, Stumble, Tumble’ is a feature of
Medicine-01.exp:
“Mumble, stumble, tumble” is a classic feature of moderate hypothermia due to progressive impairment of the central nervous system.

Features of moderate hypothermia (core temperature ~28–32°C):

  • Mumble → Slurred speech due to CNS dysfunction

  • Stumble → Ataxia and impaired coordination

  • Tumble → Falls due to muscle weakness and poor balance

  • Confusion and drowsiness may occur

  • Mild hypothermia: Mainly causes shivering, cold sensation, and mild confusion.

  • Severe hypothermia: Causes coma, severe bradycardia, arrhythmias, and reduced consciousness.

  • Trench foot: Cold-induced injury due to prolonged exposure to wet conditions, mainly affecting feet.

Exam Pearl:
“Mumble, stumble, tumble” → Moderate hypothermia (CNS impairment).

Medicine-01.question: ২২) Muscle function and global nutritional status is measured by
Medicine-01.exp:
Hand grip strength is used to assess muscle function and global nutritional status. It is a simple functional measure of muscle strength, reflecting overall body protein status and nutritional reserve.

  • Waist : hip ratio: Assesses fat distribution and cardiovascular risk, not muscle function.

  • Bioelectrical impedance: Estimates body composition (fat mass, lean mass, body water), but does not directly measure muscle function.

  • Triceps skin fold thickness: Measures subcutaneous fat stores and helps assess energy reserves, but not muscle function.

Exam Pearl:
Muscle function + nutritional status assessment → Hand grip strength.

Medicine-01.question: ২৩) Sudden onset of Unilateral pleuritic chest pain with absent breath sound & resonant hemithorax
Medicine-01.exp:
Sudden onset unilateral pleuritic chest pain + absent breath sounds + resonant (hyper-resonant) hemithorax is a classic presentation of pneumothorax, and when associated with pressure effects it indicates tension pneumothorax.

Features of tension pneumothorax:

  • Sudden severe unilateral chest pain and dyspnoea

  • Absent breath sounds on affected side

  • Hyper-resonant percussion note

  • Tracheal deviation (late sign)

  • Hypotension and shock due to impaired venous return

  • ALVF (Acute left ventricular failure): Causes pulmonary edema with bilateral crackles, not unilateral absent breath sounds.

  • MI: Causes central crushing chest pain, not hyper-resonant hemithorax.

  • MS (Mitral stenosis): Causes pulmonary congestion and dyspnoea, not these acute signs.

Exam Pearl:
Absent breath sound + hyper-resonant chest + sudden pleuritic pain → Pneumothorax (tension if unstable).

Medicine-01.question: ২৪) Barking cough is found in
Medicine-01.exp:
A barking cough is classically associated with upper airway obstruction, especially croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) and may be described in acute epiglottitis in some exam contexts. It occurs due to inflammation and narrowing of the upper airway.

  • Lung abscess: Causes productive cough with foul-smelling sputum, fever, and toxicity.

  • Bronchiectasis: Causes chronic productive cough with large amounts of purulent sputum.

  • ALVF (Acute left ventricular failure): Causes cough with breathlessness and pulmonary edema, sometimes pink frothy sputum, not barking cough.

Exam Pearl:
Barking cough → Upper airway obstruction (classically croup/epiglottitis).

Medicine-01.question: ২৫) GIT cause of cough
২৬) Vomiting without nausea is found in
Medicine-01.exp:
Vomiting without nausea (often projectile vomiting) is a classic feature of raised intracranial pressure (ICP). It occurs due to stimulation of the vomiting centre in the medulla by increased intracranial pressure, commonly seen in brain tumours or intracranial lesions.

Features of raised ICP:

  • Early morning headache

  • Projectile vomiting without nausea

  • Papilloedema

  • Visual disturbances

  • Altered consciousness (late)

  • GOO (Gastric outlet obstruction): Causes vomiting, usually with nausea, early satiety, and retained food particles.

  • PUD: May cause vomiting due to obstruction or complications, but nausea is usually present.

  • GERD: Causes regurgitation and heartburn, not typically vomiting without nausea.

Exam Pearl:
Projectile vomiting without nausea → Raised intracranial pressure.

Medicine-01.question: ২৭) Anemia with HTN & oedema
২৮) Long standing jaundice with itching, pigmentation of skin
Medicine-01.exp:
Long-standing jaundice with itching (pruritus) and skin pigmentation is classically seen in Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC), a chronic autoimmune disease causing progressive destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts.

Features of PBC:

  • Chronic cholestatic jaundice

  • Severe pruritus due to bile salt deposition

  • Hyperpigmentation of skin

  • Xanthelasma/xanthoma

  • Middle-aged women commonly affected

  • Positive anti-mitochondrial antibody (AMA)

  • PSC (Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis): Causes cholestatic jaundice but is more associated with IBD (especially ulcerative colitis) and affects intra & extrahepatic bile ducts.

  • Obstructive jaundice: Causes itching but usually due to mechanical obstruction (e.g., stone, tumour).

  • Acute viral hepatitis: Causes acute jaundice with malaise, not chronic pruritus and pigmentation.

Exam Pearl:
Chronic cholestatic jaundice + pruritus + pigmentation → PBC.

Medicine-01.question: ২৯) Most effective laparoscopic bariatric surgical procedure
৩০) Essential amino acid excludes
৩১) Which visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells?
Medicine-01.exp:
PET scan is used to visualize the metabolic activity of tumour cells. It commonly uses 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG), a glucose analogue taken up more by metabolically active cancer cells due to increased glucose metabolism.

Uses of PET:

  • Detection of primary tumour activity

  • Staging of cancer

  • Detection of metastasis

  • Monitoring response to treatment

  • CT: Provides anatomical details (size, shape, location of tumour).

  • MRI: Gives excellent soft tissue imaging but does not primarily assess metabolism.

  • Isotope scanning: Detects specific organ function or bone lesions but is not the standard for tumour metabolic activity.

Exam Pearl:
Tumour metabolic activity → FDG-PET scan.

Medicine-01.question: ৩২) Which remains the most important part of the clinical decision-making process?
Medicine-01.exp:
History taking remains the most important part of the clinical decision-making process because it provides the majority of diagnostic information and guides further examination and investigations.

A good history helps to:

  • Identify the likely diagnosis

  • Understand the onset, progression, and severity of disease

  • Decide which examinations and investigations are required

  • Avoid unnecessary tests

  • General examination: Provides important clinical signs but is supportive.

  • Systemic examination: Helps confirm and refine the diagnosis.

  • Investigation reports: Support diagnosis but should be interpreted in the context of history and examination.

Exam Pearl:
Clinical diagnosis begins with history → then examination → then investigations

Medicine-01.question: ৩৩) Jaundice with high fever and urinary complain indicates
Medicine-01.exp:
Jaundice with high fever and urinary complaints is suggestive of leptospirosis (Weil’s disease), a severe form of infection caused by Leptospira interrogans.

Features include:

  • High fever with chills

  • Jaundice due to hepatic involvement

  • Renal involvement → oliguria, renal failure, urinary abnormalities

  • Myalgia (especially calf muscle pain)

  • Conjunctival suffusion

  • Gilbert’s syndrome: Causes mild intermittent unconjugated jaundice without fever or urinary symptoms.

  • Wilson’s disease: Causes chronic liver disease with neurological features; not typically high fever with urinary complaints.

  • Hemochromatosis: Causes chronic liver disease, diabetes, and pigmentation, not acute fever.

Exam Pearl:
Jaundice + high fever + renal/urinary involvement → Leptospirosis (Weil’s disease).

Medicine-01.question: ৩৪) Weight loss with pigmentation and hypotension
Medicine-01.exp:
Weight loss + skin pigmentation + hypotension is a classic triad of Addison’s disease (primary adrenal insufficiency).

Mechanism:

  • Weight loss: Due to deficiency of cortisol causing reduced appetite and increased catabolism.

  • Hyperpigmentation: Due to increased ACTH secretion, which stimulates melanocytes (ACTH shares a precursor with MSH).

  • Hypotension: Due to deficiency of aldosterone and cortisol, causing sodium loss and reduced vascular tone.

  • Thyrotoxicosis: Causes weight loss and heat intolerance but usually causes normal/increased BP, not pigmentation.

  • DM: Causes weight loss due to insulin deficiency but not skin pigmentation with hypotension.

  • Malabsorption syndrome: Causes weight loss and nutritional deficiencies but not characteristic pigmentation and hypotension.

Exam Pearl:
Weight loss + hyperpigmentation + hypotension → Addison’s disease (primary adrenal insufficiency).

Medicine-01.question: ৩৫) Extreme cachexia in young female with history of diet control, heavy exercise and amenorrhea
Medicine-01.exp:
Extreme cachexia in a young female with strict diet control, excessive exercise, and amenorrhea is classic for anorexia nervosa, an eating disorder characterized by self-induced weight loss due to distorted body image.

Features:

  • Severe weight loss/cachexia

  • Excessive dieting and exercise

  • Amenorrhea due to hypothalamic suppression and reduced GnRH secretion

  • Bradycardia, hypotension, and endocrine abnormalities may occur

  • Bulimia nervosa: Characterized by recurrent binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors (vomiting, laxatives, excessive exercise); body weight is often normal.

  • Malignancy: Can cause cachexia but not typically associated with deliberate diet restriction and excessive exercise.

  • Ectopic pregnancy: Causes abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding, not chronic cachexia.

Exam Pearl:
Young female + severe weight loss + excessive exercise/dieting + amenorrhea → Anorexia nervosa.

Medicine-01.question: ৩৬) Headache indicates … cause of weight gain?
Medicine-01.exp:
Headache associated with weight gain suggests a pituitary cause, especially a pituitary tumour (e.g., Cushing disease due to ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma).

Mechanism:

  • Pituitary tumours can cause headache due to mass effect on surrounding structures.

  • Hormonal excess (e.g., ACTH excess) may lead to weight gain, central obesity, and other endocrine features.

  • Adrenal: Cushing syndrome causes weight gain, but headache is not a typical primary feature.

  • Ovarian: PCOS may cause weight gain but not usually headache due to mass effect.

  • Thyroid: Hypothyroidism causes weight gain but headache is not a characteristic clue.

Exam Pearl:
Headache + endocrine symptoms (especially weight gain) → Think pituitary pathology.

Medicine-01.question: ৩৭) Endocrine factors causing weight gain excludes
৩৮) Minimum BMI for being obese in Asians
Medicine-01.exp:
According to WHO Asian criteria, the BMI cutoff for obesity in Asians is lower than the standard WHO criteria because Asians develop metabolic complications (especially diabetes and cardiovascular disease) at lower BMI values.

BMI classification in Asians:

  • Normal: 18.5 – 22.9 kg/m²

  • Overweight: ≥23 kg/m²

  • Obesity: ≥25 kg/m² (Asian cut-off)

However, in many exam settings, when asking the minimum BMI for being obese, the expected answer is 25.

Options given:

  • 23 → Overweight (Asian cut-off)

  • 25 → Obesity (Asian cut-off) ✅

  • 30 → Obesity (general WHO cut-off for all populations)

  • 40 → Morbid obesity

Correct MCQ Answer: খ) 25

Exam Pearl:
Asian obesity cutoff BMI ≥25 kg/m²; overweight starts at BMI ≥23 kg/m².

Medicine-01.question: ৩৯) Pellagra occurs due to deficiency of which vitamin?
Medicine-01.exp:
Pellagra occurs due to deficiency of niacin (Vitamin B3) or its precursor tryptophan.

Classical features of pellagra are the “3 Ds”:

  • Dermatitis → photosensitive, rough skin lesions

  • Diarrhoea → gastrointestinal symptoms

  • Dementia → neurological changes
    (Severe untreated cases may lead to death — the 4th D)

  • Vitamin A deficiency: Causes night blindness and xerophthalmia.

  • Vitamin E deficiency: Causes neuropathy and haemolytic anaemia.

  • Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency: Causes beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy.

Exam Pearl:
Pellagra = Niacin (Vitamin B3) deficiency → “3 Ds: Dermatitis, Diarrhoea, Dementia.”

Medicine-01.question: ৪০) Dermatitis is a deficiency feature of vitamin…?
৪১) Cardiomyopathy results from deficiency of
৪২) Black tongue is a feature of
Medicine-01.exp:
Black tongue is a classic feature of bismuth poisoning due to the formation of bismuth sulfide in the mouth, which causes dark pigmentation of the tongue and oral mucosa.

Features of bismuth toxicity:

  • Black discoloration of tongue

  • Darkening of gums/oral mucosa

  • GI upset (nausea, constipation) in some cases

  • CO poisoning: Causes headache, dizziness, confusion, and cherry-red skin (classically described), not black tongue.

  • Lead poisoning: Causes Burton’s blue line on gums, abdominal colic, anaemia, and neuropathy.

  • Calcium excess: Causes hypercalcaemia symptoms, not tongue pigmentation.

Exam Pearl:
Black tongue → Bismuth toxicity (bismuth sulfide deposition).

Medicine-01.question: ৪৩) ‘Corkscrew hairs’ found in
Medicine-01.exp:
“Corkscrew hairs” are a classic feature of Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy). Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis, and deficiency causes defective connective tissue formation affecting hair follicles.

Features of scurvy:

  • Corkscrew hairs (twisted, fragile hairs due to follicular abnormalities)

  • Bleeding gums

  • Easy bruising and petechiae

  • Poor wound healing

  • Bone pain

  • Vitamin A deficiency: Causes night blindness, xerophthalmia, and dry skin.

  • Severe malnutrition: May cause hair changes (e.g., flag sign), but corkscrew hairs are specifically linked to vitamin C deficiency.

  • Vitamin B1 deficiency: Causes beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy.

Exam Pearl:
Corkscrew hairs + bleeding gums → Vitamin C deficiency (Scurvy).

Medicine-01.question: ৪৪) The tendency towards inaction, rooted in the principle of ‘first do no harm.’ Indicates-
Medicine-01.exp:
Omission bias refers to the tendency to prefer inaction (doing nothing) over taking action because the potential harm caused by an action is perceived as worse than harm caused by inaction.

In medical ethics, it is often linked with the principle “first do no harm” (primum non nocere), where clinicians may avoid an intervention due to fear of causing harm, even when action may be beneficial.

  • Commission bias: The tendency to prefer taking action or doing something, even when observation or waiting may be better.

  • Hindsight bias: Believing after an event that the outcome was predictable (“I knew it all along”).

  • Confirmation bias: Seeking or interpreting information that supports one’s existing beliefs while ignoring conflicting evidence.

Exam Pearl:
Preference for doing nothing due to fear of harm → Omission bias.

Medicine-01.question: ৪৫) Splinter hemorrhage in nail indicates
Medicine-01.exp:
Splinter hemorrhages are a classic peripheral sign of subacute bacterial endocarditis. They appear as small, linear, red-brown streaks under the nails due to microvascular damage caused by septic emboli.

Features of SBE:

  • Low-grade fever

  • Fatigue and weight loss

  • Splinter hemorrhages

  • Osler nodes

  • Janeway lesions

  • Roth spots

  • NS (Nephrotic syndrome): Causes oedema, proteinuria, and hypoalbuminaemia; not splinter hemorrhages.

  • PEM (Protein-energy malnutrition): Causes muscle wasting, oedema, and hair/skin changes.

  • Psoriasis: Can cause nail pitting, onycholysis, and subungual hyperkeratosis, but not classic splinter hemorrhages.

Exam Pearl:
Splinter hemorrhage + fever → Infective endocarditis (especially subacute bacterial endocarditis).

Medicine-01.question: ৪৬) The hypothalamus normally maintains core temperature at
Medicine-01.exp:
The hypothalamus acts as the body’s thermoregulatory centre and normally maintains the core body temperature around 37°C (set point).

Mechanism:

  • The preoptic area of the anterior hypothalamus regulates heat loss.

  • The posterior hypothalamus controls heat production and conservation.

  • It maintains balance between heat production and heat loss.

  • 35°C: Indicates mild hypothermia.

  • 36°C: Lower than normal core temperature.

  • 39°C: Fever/hyperthermia range.

Exam Pearl:
Hypothalamic temperature set point → approximately 37°C.

Medicine-01.question: ৪৭) Characteristic ECG wave in hypothermia
Medicine-01.exp:
The characteristic ECG finding in hypothermia is the J wave (Osborn wave).

Features of hypothermia on ECG:

  • J (Osborn) wave — positive deflection at the junction of QRS complex and ST segment

  • Sinus bradycardia

  • Prolonged PR, QRS, and QT intervals

  • Atrial and ventricular arrhythmias in severe cases

  • S wave: Not a characteristic hypothermia finding.

  • Delta wave: Seen in Wolff–Parkinson–White (WPW) syndrome due to accessory pathway conduction.

  • F wave: Seen in atrial fibrillation (fibrillatory waves).

Exam Pearl:
Hypothermia ECG → J (Osborn) wave.

Medicine-01.question: ৪৮) Freezing cold injury
Medicine-01.exp:
Frostbite is a freezing cold injury caused by exposure of tissues to temperatures below freezing, leading to ice crystal formation within cells and blood vessels, causing tissue damage.

Features of frostbite:

  • Numbness and pain

  • Pale, hard, waxy skin

  • Blister formation after rewarming

  • Severe cases → tissue necrosis and gangrene

  • Chilblains (pernio): Inflammatory skin lesions caused by prolonged exposure to cold but not freezing temperatures.

  • Trench foot / Immersion foot: Non-freezing cold injuries caused by prolonged exposure to cold, wet conditions.

Exam Pearl:
Freezing cold injury → Frostbite.
Wet cold exposure without freezing → Trench foot / Immersion foot

Medicine-01.question: ৪৯) Facial expression in hyperthyroidism
৫০) Delayed relaxation of grip indicates
Medicine-01.exp:
Delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes (including grip relaxation) is a classic sign of hypothyroidism. It occurs due to slowed metabolism and impaired muscle contraction–relaxation processes caused by deficiency of thyroid hormones.

Features of hypothyroidism:

  • Delayed relaxation phase of ankle jerk and grip reflex

  • Fatigue and lethargy

  • Weight gain

  • Cold intolerance

  • Dry skin

  • Bradycardia

  • Myotonic dystrophy: Causes delayed muscle relaxation (myotonia) after voluntary contraction, but it is not the classic endocrine association in this question.

  • Depression: May cause psychomotor slowing but not delayed reflex relaxation.

  • Anxiety: Causes increased sympathetic activity, not delayed relaxation.

Exam Pearl:
Delayed relaxation of reflexes → Hypothyroidism (classic sign).
